description: Replace the DMS-983 terminal-stage seam with an executor-facing write request for DMS-984. Acceptance: `RelationalDocumentStoreRepository` selects the active `MappingSet`, `ResourceWritePlan`, and, for existing-document flows, the `ResourceReadPlan`, then hands one executor request into a new relational write executor service instead of calling the reference resolver, flattener, and terminal stage directly. Introduce executor-facing contracts that carry the selected body, operation kind, target lookup result, mapping-set-scoped plans, trace metadata, and any executor-only diagnostics without forcing later runtime stages to rediscover them. `FlatteningInput`, `FlattenedWriteSet`, and the candidate row-buffer contracts remain usable by the executor, but `IRelationalWriteTerminalStage` is removed or demoted so it is no longer the architectural boundary for persistence orchestration.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests that prove the repository still enforces write-plan/read-plan guard rails, shapes the new executor request correctly, and no longer constructs `FlatteningInput` itself.

description: Replace the temporary PUT target-resolution seam with operation-correct lookup semantics. Acceptance: POST lookup returns either `CreateNew` or `ExistingDocument`; PUT lookup returns either `ExistingDocument` or `NotFound`; existing-document lookup includes `DocumentId`, `DocumentUuid`, and the observed `ContentVersion`; `RelationalWriteTargetContext` remains executor-facing and only models real write targets (`CreateNew` or `ExistingDocument`); `UpdateDocumentById` short-circuits missing PUT targets to `UpdateFailureNotExists` before reference resolution, flattening, current-state load, or executor execution; legacy behavior that converted missing PUT targets into `CreateNew` is removed from both production code and tests.
steps-to-verify: Add unit tests for POST create-vs-update lookup, PUT existing-vs-not-found lookup, and repository short-circuit mapping to `UpdateFailureNotExists`.

description: Introduce a request-scoped relational write session that owns one open connection and transaction per executor attempt. Acceptance: the write executor can use a shared connection/transaction for prerequisite lookups, current-state hydration, `CollectionItemId` reservation, and final DML on both PostgreSQL and SQL Server; commit and rollback are explicit and attempt-scoped; the old one-command-one-connection pattern no longer dictates write orchestration; low-level command executors may remain as utilities, but orchestration no longer depends on them as the primary seam.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests for session lifecycle, commit/rollback behavior, and dialect selection for executor attempts.

description: Move request-scoped reference resolution and flattener invocation under the write executor so they can share the executor-owned session. Acceptance: the executor resolves document and descriptor references through the shared session without opening independent connections, preserves existing request-local memoization and reference-failure classification semantics, and only calls the flattener after reference resolution succeeds. The flattener still receives the same backend-local contracts and remains pure request-body to row-buffer transformation. Reference failures still short-circuit before any DML is issued and continue to map to the current public `UpsertFailureReference` and `UpdateFailureReference` results.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests that prove the executor resolves references before flattening, preserves memoization behavior, and exits before DML on reference failures.

description: Add a write-path-local, session-aware current-state loader for one existing document using the compiled read plan and `HydrationExecutor`. Acceptance: DMS-984 can load `DocumentMetadataRow` plus hydrated table rows for a single `DocumentId` through the executor-owned connection/transaction using `PageKeysetSpec.Single`; the loader is narrow and rowset-first, with no profile projection or JSON reconstitution requirements; public `IDocumentHydrator` stays unchanged for the read path; existing-document write attempts fail deterministically when a required `ResourceReadPlan` is missing; the loaded current state is reusable by both guarded no-op comparison and later DMS-1105 work.
steps-to-verify: Add backend or plans tests that prove an existing-document write attempt can materialize current metadata plus table rows from the selected read plan without opening a second connection seam.

description: Implement the shared no-profile post-merge rowset synthesis and guarded no-op comparison path for existing-document writes. Acceptance: PUT and POST-as-update use one shared helper for merge matching, deterministic sibling ordering, compare projection, and no-op equality rather than separate compare-only logic; comparison consumes `CollectionMergePlan.CompareBindingIndexesInOrder` and the same stable-identity metadata used by the real executor; unchanged writes short-circuit as guarded no-ops without issuing DML or bumping `dms.Document.ContentVersion`; existing-document writes only proceed when the post-merge identity projection matches the stored identity projection; `allowIdentityUpdates=false` yields the normal immutable-identity failure path, while `allowIdentityUpdates=true` yields a deterministic not-yet-supported failure until the E09 identity-maintenance stories land.
steps-to-verify: Add backend and plans unit tests for unchanged PUT, unchanged POST-as-update, compare-order reuse, identity-stable matching, and identity-changing guard rails.

description: Introduce internal executor attempt outcomes and repository-level stale-no-op handling. Acceptance: the executor returns internal attempt results such as applied write, guarded no-op, and stale no-op compare rather than only public `UpsertResult` and `UpdateResult`; the repository maps successful attempts back to `InsertSuccess`, `UpdateSuccess`, or successful PUT responses; when a no-op compare goes stale and there is no external `If-Match` policy yet, the repository reruns exactly one full executor attempt against fresh state; if the retry also goes stale or hits retryable contention, the request maps to a write-conflict outcome rather than returning success from stale state; the internal stale result remains reusable by DMS-1005 later.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests for stale-no-op classification, one-time retry behavior, and result mapping back to public repository outcomes.

description: Implement transactional DML for `dms.Document`, the resource root row, root extension rows, and non-collection separate-table or inlined scopes on the no-profile path. Acceptance: create flows insert `dms.Document` and the required relational rows in dependency order; update flows update matched rows, insert newly present separate-table rows, delete omitted separate-table rows, and clear compiled bindings for omitted inlined scopes instead of preserving hidden data; no-profile root `_ext` rows and aligned one-to-one extension scopes follow the same present/absent semantics as base data; the executor commits all changed rows in one transaction and rolls back fully on failure with no partial writes left behind.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests for non-collection present/absent handling, inlined clear behavior, root extension row handling, and rollback-on-failure behavior using an injected failure hook.

description: Implement stable-identity collection/common-type/extension-collection merge execution for no-profile writes. Acceptance: the executor loads the current sibling set from the current-state loader, matches request candidates to stored rows by compiled semantic identity, updates matched rows in place, deletes omitted rows by stable row identity, reserves new `CollectionItemId` values only for unmatched inserts, and applies the same logic to nested collections, root-level extension child collections, and collection-aligned extension child collections. `Ordinal` recomputation uses the same deterministic post-merge ordering helper used by the guarded no-op compare path. `FullSurfaceCollectionReorder` must prove matched rows keep their existing `CollectionItemId` values while only `Ordinal` changes.
steps-to-verify: Add backend and plans unit tests for semantic-identity matching, matched-row preservation, delete-plus-insert on identity changes, ordinal recomputation, and extension child collection handling.

description: Implement batched relational DML that respects dialect-specific parameter limits without introducing provider-specific bulk-loader paths in this story. Acceptance: inserts and updates are grouped to avoid N+1 execution patterns; multi-row insert chunking and parameter partitioning honor PostgreSQL and SQL Server parameter limits; `CollectionItemId` reservation is batched by table or scope as needed; large collections that exceed one batch are persisted through multiple bounded batches inside the same transaction; provider-specific `COPY` and `SqlBulkCopy` optimizations remain out of scope for DMS-984.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests for batch partitioning decisions, parameter-limit handling, and multi-batch collection insert behavior.

description: Add fast verification coverage for DMS-984 orchestration and dialect-specific contract behavior. Acceptance: backend unit tests cover target lookup mapping, executor request shaping, session lifecycle, reference-resolution short-circuiting, stale-no-op retry policy, identity-stability guard rails, non-collection present/absent semantics, collection match classification, and batch partitioning. Plans unit tests cover stable merge metadata consumption, compare-order reuse, and deterministic no-op projection behavior. SQL Server receives a smaller safety net in unit or contract coverage for generated SQL and batching behavior without requiring full SQL Server end-to-end integration in this story.

Add end-to-end PostgreSQL integration coverage for the DMS-984 no-profile runtime baseline using compiled schema and plan fixtures rather than hand-written table definitions. Acceptance: integration tests cover `NoProfileWriteBehavior` with changed writes, nested collections, omitted non-collection scope semantics, no-profile `_ext` handling, PUT update, and POST-as-update; `FullSurfaceCollectionReorder` proving stable `CollectionItemId` preservation plus ordinal recomputation; unchanged PUT and unchanged POST-as-update guarded no-op behavior with unchanged `dms.Document.ContentVersion`; stale compare recheck with a concurrent content-version bump; batch-threshold crossing for large collections; and rollback verification proving no partial rows commit when an injected failure occurs. Assertions are database-first: actual rows, delete-vs-clear semantics, `CollectionItemId` reuse, `Ordinal` values, and changed-vs-unchanged `ContentVersion` behavior.
steps-to-verify: Add PostgreSQL integration tests that provision the compiled relational model, execute the write path through the repository and executor, and assert directly against database state for the accepted scenario names.
